guide.title: Build a complete practice conversation.
guide.lead: Prepare a room, generate its opening, continue with learner turns and save the closeout.
guide.intro: **Add the Conversations API to your workspace.** Sign in, review the current terms and rate, then add this API. Fund live usage and create a scoped server key in the console.

sections.title: 1. Select a room and its participants
2. Open the room and continue
Show how each character responds (optional)
sections.markdown:
## Show how each character responds (optional)

Every saved turn includes `characters`, one entry per cast member, so your app can change a portrait or show an empty seat. Using them is optional; nothing else depends on them.

- `presence` is `present`, `stepped_away` or `left`. Characters can step out and return, and someone pushed too far can leave for the rest of the session.
- `expression_group` is the simpler set: `steady_and_engaged`, `more_open`, `more_careful`, `more_strained` or `participating_less`. Five portraits per character are enough.
- `expression` is the detailed state, one of 16, for finer portraits. Each belongs to one group, listed in the OpenAPI.

Both are `null` when no expression was reported, including during a safety moment: show the neutral portrait. These are simulated cast responses, not a reading of a real person. Show them as faces or cues rather than labels, so your users practice reading people.

sections.title: 3. Return to saved practice
sections.markdown:
## 3. Return to saved practice

Read the session, paged playback, debrief and cross-session insights under `/v1/conversation`. These reads make no new generation purchase. Use the returned cursor to continue playback. Debrief becomes available when the practice closes.

Every saved turn includes stable speaker identities, its original controls and explicit structure availability. When attribution is unavailable, show the saved text without inventing a speaker. Debriefs describe the recorded practice, its conditions and the moments that mattered.

sections.title: 4. Add optional whole-turn audio
sections.markdown:
## 4. Add optional whole-turn audio

The audio contract accepts a saved session and turn, never arbitrary text. `POST /v1/conversation/voice` with `operation: "generate"` creates one generation covering participating cast and Coach. A retry retrieves the same saved or pending generation.

A `202` response means the generation is pending. Save its `audio_id`. To continue, send `POST /v1/conversation/audio/AUDIO_ID/continue` with the same user and assignment, using a key with `chat` and `sessions:read` scopes. Respect `Retry-After`. Each request advances at most one segment of that existing purchase. Stop on a terminal status; a failed generation has no audio charge.

Find existing generations with `GET /v1/conversation/sessions/SESSION_ID/audio`, following its pagination cursor. `GET /v1/conversation/audio/AUDIO_ID` reads current status. Neither read creates or continues speech generation.

Fetch saved segment URLs through your authenticated server. Audio expires 24 hours after creation; playback does not extend that time or synthesize again. A segment fetched after expiry returns `410` `AUDIO_EXPIRED`. Use explicit `regenerate`, a new operation key and `replaces_audio_id` for a new purchase.

sections.title: 5. Provide export and deletion
sections.markdown:
## 5. Provide export and deletion

Export paged saved turns, setup, consent, preferences, practice summaries and audio-generation metadata with `POST /v1/conversation/data/export`. Export requires its dedicated key scope. Download available recordings through their authenticated audio routes before expiry. Session deletion also removes session-derived memory and saved audio. End-user erasure covers the user’s practice data; content-free financial records remain.

Deletion immediately revokes content access. A `202` receipt with `status: "pending"` means private audio cleanup is not yet confirmed. Retry the same deletion with its original `operation_id` until the receipt says `completed`.

Text retention is 180 days since activity in live mode and 30 days in test mode. Reads do not renew retention. Audio always uses its separate 24-hour creation clock.

sections.title: Contract downloads
sections.markdown:
## Contract downloads

[OpenAPI](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/openapi/conversation.openapi.json) · [Request, event and resource schemas](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/openapi/schemas/conversation-v1.schema.json)

Runnable server examples: [TypeScript](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/examples/conversation/conversation.ts) · [Python](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/examples/conversation/conversation.py) · [cURL](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/examples/conversation/conversation.sh) · [Complete workflow and recovery guide](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/examples/conversation/README.md).

Each example sends one explicit request from a saved intent, and each has offline tests. Run them free on a test assignment; add live access when you are ready.

The v1 request envelope supports 1–5 participants, 10,000 learner characters per turn and at most 100 rows per read. Every workspace includes fifty free text attempts. Your workspace shows its current rate. Request and concurrency limits apply across keys.

Keep the assigned release and returned request ID when contacting [developer support](mailto:developers@foreverlearning.ai). Saved sessions retain their original release and rate.

sections.title: One price for the whole turn.
sections.markdown:
## One price for the whole turn.

| Usage | Price | Includes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text | $0.03 per billable turn | Participating cast and Coach |
| Optional audio | +$0.05 per spoken turn | All participating voices and spoken coaching |
| Text with audio | $0.08 total | One text turn and one saved audio generation |

Ten billable text turns cost $0.30. With newly generated audio for each turn, the total is $0.80. The opening and the closeout are billable turns. The number of participants does not add a per-speaker fee. Fifty free text attempts in every workspace.

Creating an empty room and reading saved conversations, debriefs and insights do not add a generation charge. Text opening and ordinary turns bill at dispatch, with the existing refund for an observed failure before content. Generated closeout bills when saved.

Audio bills once the complete turn audio is successfully saved. Replay is free for 24 hours from creation, with earlier removal when the session or user data is deleted. Regeneration is an explicit new purchase. Audio requires available balance.

Review the rate and the free test attempts in your workspace before adding the API. These prices do not change any existing workspace assignment.

examples.name: README.md
examples.text:
# Conversations API integration examples

These clients cover the full Conversations API contract. They make **one explicitly
selected request per invocation**, with no automatic retries, voice purchases or
continuations. Add the Conversations API to your workspace in the console and
create a scoped server key before you run them; a request on a live assignment is
a purchase at your workspace's rate.

Test mode grants 50 lifetime attempts per workspace and stable Conversations listing,
shared across members and keys, at no charge. A generated opening, each reply and the
closeout debrief count, and a dispatched attempt counts even if it fails; the internal
output retry and an exact replay do not. A test assignment keeps the allowance of the
publication it was enrolled on; the console shows that figure and what remains. Test
mode is text only: audio needs a live assignment and balance. Reserve an attempt for
closeout. Exhaustion never silently switches to live charging.

Use Node 24+ for `conversation.ts`, Python 3.11+ for `conversation.py`, or Bash/Git
Bash with cURL and jq for `conversation.sh`. Each client has offline tests.

Store the API key in the server environment as `FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY`. Never
put it in a request file, browser, command-line argument, source repository or log.
Use a private local directory for request/response files: they can contain learner
content. On Windows, use your user-owned directory and its access controls.

## Save the intent before dispatch

Every request file fixes the assigned host, assignment and pseudonymous user, so
a retry cannot silently move to another environment or user. Replace these
placeholders with your approved assignment. Generate a UUID **once per new
mutation**, persist it, and retain that same ID and body on retries. A new user
action gets a new file and UUID. For lifecycle bodies, use that UUID as the
`operation_id` too.

```json
{
  "base_url": "https://ASSIGNED-API-HOST/v1",
  "assignment_id": "ASSIGNED-UUID",
  "external_user_id": "synthetic-practice-user",
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/conversation/catalog"
}
```

```sh
node conversation.ts catalog.request.json catalog.response.json
python conversation.py catalog.request.json catalog.response.json
bash conversation.sh catalog.request.json catalog-response-directory
```

Choose one client; do not run all three commands as three purchases. Each output
must be new. An empty/partial output after failure is not a completed receipt.
Recover with the unchanged request file and a new output destination. TypeScript
and Python return `{status, retry_after, data}` for JSON/SSE; audio downloads are
raw MP3 bytes. cURL saves headers, HTTP status and raw bytes. For cURL SSE, use
`parse_stream` from `conversation.py` to verify the complete stream before acting:

```sh
python -c 'from pathlib import Path; from conversation import parse_stream; print(parse_stream(Path("opening-response/response.raw").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["request_id"])'
```

For closeout, pass `True` as `parse_stream`'s second argument. No `[DONE]` sentinel
is used. HTTP 200 and provisional text alone do not establish successful billing
or saved content. The clients verify stream/session/receipt identity and safety
presence, preserve the final receipt, and refuse truncated completion.

## Complete practice flow

Keep the scope fields above in each file. These are the remaining fields/bodies;
replace IDs with catalog or prior-response values. Key scopes are cumulative:
`chat` for mutations, `sessions:read` for saved reads and audio continuation,
`data:export` for export, `data:erase` for user erasure.

| Step | Method and path | Body or query | Cost / completion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Catalog | `GET /conversation/catalog` | No body | Free; select actual room/persona IDs. |
| Prepare | `POST /conversation/sessions` | Setup example below | Free; persist `session_id` and `content_release`. |
| Opening | `POST /chat` | `{"session_id":"SESSION","conversation":{"operation":"opening"}}` | $0.03 at dispatch; no learner prompt. |
| Ordinary turn | `POST /chat` | Turn example below | $0.03 at dispatch, subject to observed-precontent refund. |
| Recover | `GET /requests/REQUEST_ID` | No body | No new generation; wait for committed outcome or retry exact original POST. |
| Read consent | `GET /conversation/sessions/SESSION/consent` | No body | Free. |
| Change consent | `POST /conversation/sessions/SESSION/consent` | `{"action":"soften"}` | Explicit revision; use the documented action enum. |
| Reopen | `GET /conversation/sessions/SESSION` | No body | Saved scope, state and current controls. |
| Playback | `GET /conversation/sessions/SESSION/playback` | `"query":{"limit":25}` | Free; follow `next_cursor`. |
| Close | `POST /sessions/SESSION/end` | `{"operation_id":"SAVED-UUID"}` | Billable generated closeout on commit; require `session_ended`. |
| Debrief | `GET /conversation/sessions/SESSION/debrief` | No body | Free; observe availability, without inventing a score. |
| Insights | `GET /conversation/insights` | No body | Free; recorded practice, not diagnoses. |
| Session list | `GET /conversation/sessions` | `"query":{"limit":25}` | Follow every opaque cursor without changing scope. |

A learner has one active session at a time. Opening the learner's next session first
closes the open one with a generated closeout, charged as a closeout ($0.03, or one
attempt in test mode), the same as calling `end`. Calling `end` is optional; call it
when you want the debrief ready before the learner's next session.

An authored setup body:

```json
{"setup":{"kind":"room","room_id":"CATALOG-ROOM","mode":"guided","participants":[{"persona_id":"CATALOG-PERSONA"}]},"controls":{"cast_language":"en-US","cast_speech":"natural","challenge":"supportive","emotional_heat":"calm"}}
```

Open practice uses `{"kind":"open","mode":"open_practice","cast_shape":"one_on_one","participants":[...] ,"topic":"A fictional team handoff"}`.
For multiple participants, choose `cast_shape:"room"`; use one to five supported
personas and the catalog's room constraints. Topic/intensive consent is explicit;
see the schemas before choosing a sensitive scenario. The practice type determines
which setup fields are accepted. Do not send consumer/private prompt documents.

An ordinary turn body:

```json
{"session_id":"SESSION","prompt":"What would help us agree on the next step?","conversation":{"operation":"turn","controls":{"challenge":"realistic","emotional_heat":"calm"}}}
```

Omitted controls retain the last saved value. The five controls are cast language,
speech style, challenge, emotional heat and coaching lens. Coach ordinarily uses
English. No fixed session turn cap applies. Request and output bounds are enforced
server-side; your workspace shows its current rate, and request and concurrency
limits apply across keys.
Emotional heat `raw` is accepted in turn controls only, as the end user's own choice.

Each `conversation_turn` carries `characters`: per cast member, `expression` (16
states), `expression_group` (five codes, the simpler set) and `presence`. They are
optional to use, for portraits or seat state; see `CONVERSATION_API.md`.

## Optional whole-turn audio

1. Explicitly request `POST /conversation/voice` with
   `{"session_id":"SESSION","turn_id":"SAVED-TURN","operation":"generate"}`.
   Persist the returned `audio_id` and original request. Only saved cast/Coach text
   can be spoken; arbitrary TTS text is not accepted.
2. On status 202/pending, respect `Retry-After`. Each explicit
   `POST /conversation/audio/AUDIO/continue` with `{}` advances at most one segment
   of the existing purchase. Do not call `voice` again with a new purchase ID to
   recover a pending generation. Stop on ready, failed or expired.
3. Read `GET /conversation/audio/AUDIO`, or discover generations using
   `GET /conversation/sessions/SESSION/audio` and its pagination cursor. Reads do
   not continue generation. Fetch a returned segment only through its authenticated
   `/conversation/audio/AUDIO/segments/SEGMENT` path on the same assigned API host.
4. The whole successful saved generation costs $0.05, including every participating
   voice and spoken Coach. Replay is free for 24 hours from creation, with earlier
   deletion. Balance is required; there is no audio grace. A failed generation has
   no audio customer charge. Internal characters do not change the customer unit.
5. Explicit regeneration uses a **new** saved intent and
   `{"session_id":"SESSION","turn_id":"SAVED-TURN","operation":"regenerate","replaces_audio_id":"AUDIO"}`.
   That is a new purchase. Text plus one successful audio generation totals $0.08.

## Privacy and deletion

`POST /conversation/data/export` uses an empty body and `"query":{"limit":25}`.
Follow `next_cursor` in subsequent query parameters until null, preserving scope.
Do not put `operation_id` or pagination in its body. Each
page returns saved setup, turns, preferences, consent, practice memory and audio
metadata; download still-available audio separately before its expiry.

`DELETE /sessions/SESSION` with `{"operation_id":"SAVED-UUID"}` deletes a session.
`POST /data/erase` with the same body shape erases the scoped API user's practice
data. These are explicit destructive choices, separate from closeout. Content
access is revoked immediately; a pending 202 receipt means audio cleanup is not
confirmed. Retry the identical lifecycle operation until `status:"completed"`.
Financial records remain. Live text retention is 180 days since activity; test
retention is 30 days. Reads do not extend retention; audio uses its own fixed clock.

The console's Sandbox namespace is separate from these API examples. Never add an
operator's internal namespace prefix to an API end-user identifier.

## Errors and support

401/403 require correcting identity, assignment or scope; 402 concerns balance or
budget; 409 can mean pending work or a stale revision; 422 can mean reused
idempotency identity with changed input; 429 requires the supplied retry guidance.
An unavailable or interrupted response remains uncertain. Resolve the original
request before a fresh purchase. Do not add automatic provider retries.

Keep the assigned release and the returned request ID when contacting developer
support at developers@foreverlearning.ai. Saved sessions retain their original
release and rate.

examples.name: conversation.ts
conversation.py
conversation.sh
examples.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# cURL + jq, Bash/Git Bash. Exactly one request, no redirects/retries.
# bash conversation.sh saved-request.json NEW-private-response-directory
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
[[ $# == 2 ]] || { echo 'Usage: bash conversation.sh saved-request.json NEW-response-directory' >&2; exit 2; }
intent=$1
destination=$2
base=$(jq -er '.base_url' "$intent")
path=$(jq -er '.path' "$intent")
method=$(jq -er '.method' "$intent")
assignment=$(jq -er '.assignment_id' "$intent")
subject=$(jq -er '.external_user_id' "$intent")
operation=$(jq -r '.idempotency_key // ""' "$intent")
[[ $base =~ ^https://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]+)?/v1/?$ ]] || { echo 'Invalid API base' >&2; exit 2; }
[[ $path =~ ^/(chat|requests/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+|sessions(/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(/(end|discard|history))?)?|session/status|data/(export|erase)|conversation/(catalog|insights|voice|data/export|sessions(/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(/(consent|playback|debrief|audio))?)?|audio/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(/(continue|segments/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+))?))$ ]] || { echo 'Invalid API path' >&2; exit 2; }
uuid='^[a-f0-9]{8}(-[a-f0-9]{4}){3}-[a-f0-9]{12}$'
[[ $assignment =~ $uuid && $method =~ ^(GET|POST|DELETE)$ ]] || exit 2
[[ -n $subject && ${#subject} -le 200 && $subject != *$'\n'* && $subject != *$'\r'* ]] || exit 2
[[ ${FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY:-} =~ ^[[:graph:]]{1,512}$ ]] || { echo 'Set the server-held key in FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY' >&2; exit 2; }
[[ $method == GET || $operation =~ $uuid ]] || { echo 'Save an operation UUID first' >&2; exit 2; }
jq -e '(.query // {}) | keys | all(. == "limit" or . == "cursor" or . == "session_id")' "$intent" >/dev/null
query=$(jq -r '(.query // {}) | to_entries | map((.key|@uri)+"="+(.value|tostring|@uri)) | join("&")' "$intent")
url=${base%/}$path
[[ -z $query ]] || url=$url?$query
# Reserve the entire output directory before any request; never overwrite a receipt.
mkdir -- "$destination"
headers=$destination/request-headers.private
trap 'rm -f -- "$headers"' EXIT
printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\nX-Assignment-Id: %s\nX-User-Id: %s\n' "$FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY" "$assignment" "$subject" >"$headers"
args=(--silent --show-error --proto '=https' --max-time 120 --max-filesize 8388608 --request "$method" --header "@$headers"
  --dump-header "$destination/response.headers" --output "$destination/response.raw" --write-out '%{http_code}')
if [[ $method != GET ]]; then
  printf 'Content-Type: application/json\nIdempotency-Key: %s\n' "$operation" >>"$headers"
  jq -c '.body // {}' "$intent" >"$destination/request-body.private"
  [[ $(wc -c <"$destination/request-body.private") -le 49152 ]] || exit 2
  args+=(--data-binary "@$destination/request-body.private")
fi
# A nonzero curl result or an error frame is ambiguous, even if some text arrived.
curl "${args[@]}" --url "$url" >"$destination/http-status"
status=$(cat "$destination/http-status")
[[ $status =~ ^2[0-9][0-9]$ ]] || { echo "HTTP $status; retain the saved request and inspect its request ID" >&2; exit 1; }
echo 'Transport finished. Verify JSON status or the final SSE receipt before another operation.'
